title: A possible role for malonyl-CoA in the regulation of hepatic fatty acid oxidation and ketogenesis
authors: McGarry JD, Mannaerts GP, Foster DW
population: Liver homogenates and mitochondrial fractions from fed and fasted rats
funder: This work was supported by U. S. Public Health Service grant AM-18573 and training grant CA 05200. J. D. McGarry held Research Career Development Award I-KO4-AM0763; G. P. Mannaerts held Fogarty International Fellowship I-FOS-TW223401.
result: Malonyl-CoA inhibited ketogenesis from oleic acid but not from octanoic acid; the site of inhibition appeared to be the carnitine acyltransferase I reaction. The effect was specific and easily reversible, and inhibitory concentrations were in the range reported by others in livers of fed rats. The authors proposed that malonyl-CoA is both precursor of fatty acid synthesis and suppressor of fatty acid oxidation.
